items.title: Process for Appointment as a Bail Commissioner
items.content_text:
MAINE JUDICIAL BRANCH 
ADA Notice: The Maine Judicial Branch complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). If you need a reasonable 
accommodation, contact the Court Access Coordinator, accessibility@courts.maine.gov, or a court clerk. 
Language Services: For language assistance and interpreters, contact a court clerk or interpreters@courts.maine.gov. 
 
CR-288, Rev. 07/26 Page 1 of 1 www.courts.maine.gov 
Process for Appointment as a Bail Commissioner   
 
 
PROCESS FOR APPOINTMENT AS A BAIL COMMISSIONER 
 
Bail Commissioners are appointed by the Chief Judge of the District Court and serve at the pleasure of the 
Court. They must be available to work on an irregular on-call schedule including nights, weekends, and 
holidays. Appointments are made after review of an application, reference calls, a background investigation, 
and a determination by the Chief Judge as to the need for a Bail Commissioner in the area where the applicant 
lives. 
 
Persons who are currently employed by, or have a family member currently employed by, the following 
agencies/businesses, are not eligible to apply: 
• A Law enforcement agency; 
• A Jail/correctional facility; 
• A Law firm; 
• The Department of Corrections; 
• A Prosecutor’s office; 
• A regional communications/dispatch center; and/or 
• A Town/City, County, State, or Federal government agency that has a law enforcement 
agency under its supervision. 
If appointed as a Bail Commissioner, each applicant must do the following before being allowed to begin their 
duties: 
• Attend a mandatory training; 
• Pass a fingerprint-based FBI criminal history background check; 
• Complete an online certification to view Criminal Justice Information; 
• Job shadow an experienced bail commissioner; and 
• Open a dedicated bail commissioner bank account.

items.title: Case Search Identifiers for Maine eCourts
items.content_text:
Table of Contents 
CASE SEARCH IDENTIFIERS FOR MAINE ECOURTS 
(Docket Numbers) 
A. MAINE ECOURTS - "GO-LIVE" DATES BY COURT LOCATION AND CASE TYPE
B. FORMAT OF THE CASE SEARCH IDENTIFIER (DOCKET NUMBER)
1. Alphabetic Prefix - Venue and Jurisdiction
a. Civil Actions - Superior Court
b. All Actions - District Court
c. Criminal and Civil Violations - Unified Criminal Docket
d. Criminal Actions - Superior Court (Pre-UCD)
2. Alphabetic Code - Type of Action/Case Type
a. Case Type Codes - Before and After Go-Live
3. Four-Digit Numerical Series - Year of Case Initiation
4. Five-Digit Sequential Number - Filing Number
C. TIPS OF FINDING A CASE IN MAINE ECOURTS
D. ADDITIONAL RESOURCES
A. MAINE ECOURTS DEPLOYMENT - "GO-LIVE" DATES BY COURT LOCATION AND CASE TYPE
The Maine Judicial Branch is in the process of rolling out an electronic filing and case management
system to the state. The "go-live" date represents the date that the efiling system is deployed and
becomes operational in each court. The following table provides the go-live date and case type(s)
associated with each court.
